issue_reference: Assigned in the registration pull request rather than guessed in advance.
hypothesis: The tournament scores a kill at five points and a coin at one, so score is coins plus five times kills. The agent's own reward table pays ten for a coin and five for a kill, valuing a kill at half a coin - a ten-fold inversion of the ratio it is graded on. It also pays five for surviving the round, which the tournament does not score at all, against minus ten for dying, so hunting is a bad trade under the reward function and a good one under the score function. That table was inherited from Task 2, where it was correct because there were no opponents to kill. Every observed result follows from it: across the line-up comparison's trajectory, training drove self-kills from 0.700 down to 0.442 and survival from 0.225 up to 0.467 while eliminations fell from 0.175 to 0.092, and score stayed flat because five-point kills were being traded for one-point coins and for survival that scores nothing. This comparison raises the elimination reward alone toward the ratio the tournament actually pays. Registered before execution: a larger elimination reward buys hunting with risk, so self-kills and survival may worsen, and the self-kill and retention gates decide whether the trade is worth taking rather than the expectation stated here.

prior_evidence.settled_factors: The dose-response selected learning rate 0.0002, the only dose in its ladder to beat the incumbent on score and hold all three retention gates. The exploration comparison kept the random-episode period at five, its response being monotone against the hypothesis that less random play is more efficient. The line-up comparison found no measurable difference between the hard and mixed training line-ups at that dose, so the mixed line-up is carried without further claim. All three are fixed for every arm here.
prior_evidence.flat_budget: The line-up comparison replayed its retained milestones on shared worlds and found score flat across a four-fold budget range - 2.650, 2.600, 3.125 and 2.950 at 600, 1,200, 1,800 and 2,400 episodes - with no peak and no decay, while self-kills and survival improved monotonically. More episodes have not bought more score; that is the evidence this comparison is built on, because it points at the objective rather than the budget.
prior_evidence.power: The unchanged incumbent scored 1.375, 1.600, 2.200, 2.350 and 3.100 on five independent forty-world sets, so no absolute score is comparable across comparisons. Every conclusion drawn here is a paired within-run contrast.

intervention.changed_factor: the elimination reward, over a registered ladder toward the tournament's own kill-to-coin ratio
intervention.baseline_shared_by_every_arm: the installed Task 3 incumbent as the starting point, the all_weights trainable scope, the mixed training line-up, native rewards with no approach shaping, one optimizer update per eligible transition, learning rate 0.0002 and one fully random episode in five
intervention.persistence: training-only; evaluation loads the unchanged archived agent
intervention.methodology_change: Registered under the changed setup: budget spent on depth rather than breadth, the trajectory retained at milestones because training is sequential and a peak that decays before the end should not be thrown away, and durable resume so an interrupted replica continues from minutes ago. Four replicas is more than the three this comparison was first drafted with, because the campaign's variance sits at the replica level and replicas are what buy power there; it is still fewer than a between-arm claim would want, and the comparison exists to choose a hyperparameter for the long run before tonight rather than to establish a small difference between arms.
intervention.registered_risk: Aligning the reward with the score function is not obviously safe. A kill is worth five points only if the agent survives to keep them, and the fifty-fold arm makes a kill worth five coins against a death costing one coin, which may buy reckless bombing. Self-kills, survival and the earlier-task retention suites are gated exactly so that a score gain bought by recklessness is caught rather than celebrated. The retained milestones are not evaluated by this run; the gates are decided on the final checkpoints.

random_episode_schedule: Every arm uses the registered #168 schedule at period five: for each block of five episodes, random.Random(agent_seed + 168000000 + block_index).randrange(5) selects one fully random episode and the other four are greedy.
primary_endpoint: Mean native score per game on classic-rule-based against the unchanged incumbent. Tournament placing is decided by score.

uncertainty.method: hierarchical paired bootstrap over replicas and shared worlds
uncertainty.family: one test family per arm that can be promoted; the promotion rule is conjunctive, so only the arm count is Bonferroni-adjusted
uncertainty.role: registered decision input, not a post-hoc description

selection: An arm is promotable only if every applicable integrity gate, every retention gate and every efficacy gate passes. Among promotable arms the largest mean score gain over the unchanged incumbent is chosen, and within it the median-final replica by that score. The best-looking replica is not selectable. If no arm is promotable the installed incumbent remains the submission candidate.
scientific_gates: Original cumulative Task 1/2/3 requirements are unchanged; this exploratory comparison cannot retrospectively establish any of them.
known_gate_defect: The frozen_online_weights gate is reported as not applicable, because every arm registers the scope whose purpose is to move those weights. The invalid-action gate compares each trained artifact against the unchanged reference rather than demanding a global zero it could never reach; every completed Task 4 comparison has failed it, which is a finding about fine-tuning rather than a discriminator between arms.

machine_allocation.training: 5 concurrent workers, one torch thread each
machine_allocation.latency: one worker on an otherwise idle machine; the only latency source

authorization: Owner 1BlauNitrox authorized this comparison on 16 September 2026 as the last Task 4 screen before the long training run, to decide the replay capacity that run is configured with. No automatic extension, no automatic promotion; the README and interpretation follow completed results.
